text: For a smallholder farmer in Preah Vihear, basic poultry care (chickens and ducks) depends on adequate feed, reliable clean water, suitable shelter, ventilation, protection from predators and weather, and daily observation. Grain alone is generally not nutritionally complete, particularly for rapidly growing chicks or laying hens — birds need energy, protein/amino acids, minerals, vitamins, and water. Requirements change with production stage (chicks, growing birds, layers, meat birds, breeders), so ask what kind of bird and production purpose before giving feeding advice. Chicks are especially vulnerable to cold, wet conditions, predators, overcrowding, and competition. During the wet season (roughly May–October), housing should stay dry and protected from rain; wet litter should be managed promptly since damp conditions increase disease/parasite risk, but ventilation still matters even while keeping rain out. During the dry season (roughly November–April), heat is the major concern — birds need shade, ventilation, and reliable clean water, with unnecessary handling avoided during the hottest periods. Feeders and drinkers should stay clean and positioned to reduce contamination. A sudden drop in feed/water consumption or egg production is an early warning sign. Free-ranging/scavenging systems are common for smallholders and reduce feed cost but increase exposure to predators, wild birds, and disease — do not automatically recommend full confinement. There is not enough province-specific evidence to name one predominant Preah Vihear chicken breed — record the farmer's actual type (local/native, improved, broiler, layer, duck) rather than guessing. Practical foundation: safe feed → clean water → dry shelter → shade/ventilation → predator protection → cleanliness → daily observation → appropriate veterinary/vaccination support. Do not invent homemade ration percentages without appropriate nutritional validation.
